answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists Sybil attacks: every agent must lock a bond before trading, and each honest deal adds weight while fraud slashes it. New identities start at zero trust, so an attacker spawning thousands of clones gains nothing — each clone must earn its record from scratch. Like light through a prism, one honest history splits into many verifiable signals, while a whisper network of peers flags sudden clusters of identical newcomers. Onyx-grade finality comes from the bond itself: faking an identity is cheap, but faking a long, costly track record is not.
